headline: The Efficiency Winner Takes All
subtitle: Anthropic dethrones OpenAI on unit economics, enterprises demand AI verification, and domain experts become irreplaceable.
editorial_intro: Three signals are converging that will reshape who wins in AI: capital is flowing to efficiency, not raw capability. Trust is collapsing without verification. And expertise is becoming the asymmetric amplifier that separates god-tier practitioners from commodified juniors. This isn't about better models anymore — it's about who can deliver reliable output at sustainable cost.

signals.headline: Anthropic Becomes Most Valuable AI Company on Unit Economics Play
signals.body: Anthropic has surpassed OpenAI in valuation ($965B) while shipping Claude Opus 4.8 alongside Claude Mythos, a new model class arriving in weeks. This isn't about capability breakthroughs — it's a signal that Anthropic has solved the cost-per-output problem that's rationing AI spend across corporate America. When the market values efficiency over raw power, the competitive landscape inverts.
signals.whycare: Stop watching capability benchmarks. Start tracking unit economics and inference costs — that's where competitive advantage lives now. If Anthropic's valuation lead holds, expect the entire industry to pivot from bigger-is-better to efficient-is-winning within 12 months.

signals.headline: EY's Hallucination Crisis Makes Unverified AI Output Uninsurable
signals.body: EY published a cybersecurity report with most citations hallucinated — a Big Four firm released AI-generated work downstream without verification. This signals AI-generated content is crossing into high-stakes domains (regulatory reports, compliance guidance) without gatekeeping. Expect this to trigger contractual language changes and spawn new product categories around AI auditability.
signals.whycare: Demand citation-level provenance and verification on any AI-generated work touching compliance or risk. Insurance carriers will soon make this contractual — get ahead of it now or face liability questions in 90 days.

signals.headline: Domain Expertise Becomes the Asymmetric Amplifier
signals.body: Claude Mythos is compressing penetration testing from years to weeks, and the pattern is clear: a domain expert with advanced AI can accomplish god-tier work, while a junior generalist without domain knowledge races toward commodification. Capability is plateauing across models — the winner isn't the smartest AI, it's the practitioner who can describe complex problems clearly enough for AI to solve autonomously.
signals.whycare: Invest in deepening expertise in your core domain — it's becoming scarcer, not commoditized. If you're hiring or building teams, prioritize people who understand problem decomposition over people who chase prompt-engineering trends.

bigger_picture: The AI market is hitting an inflection point where capability has plateaued but cost and trustworthiness have not. Capital is rewarding efficiency over raw power, enterprises are demanding verification before deploying AI output, and skill development is shifting from "how do I prompt this?" to "how do I define tasks clearly for autonomous execution?" This creates two winners: vendors who crack reliable, auditable inference at scale, and practitioners with deep domain expertise who can leverage AI as a 10x amplifier. Everyone else faces commodification pressure. The next 12 months will separate the market leaders from the feature-followers through ruthless competition on efficiency and trustworthiness — not benchmark scores.
